newsitem.title: USA: IMF official concerned about emerging market value.
newsitem.headline: IMF official concerned about emerging market value.

text.p: Although emerging markets have shown phenomenal growth in recent years, a top International Monetary Fund official warned Friday that such markets may be currently overvalued.

Jack Boorman, director of the policy development and review department at the IMF, observed that emerging market bonds are trading at rates close to bonds of developed countries and stocks are trading at high valuations.
Boorman said the narrowness of spreads in some markets and heightened valuations of stocks in some countries were a cause for concern.

"You have to wonder whether or not there isn't a mass psychology of the kind that took place among the commercial banks in the 1970s and early 1980s that is setting somebody up for some difficulty," Boorman said at a conference sponsored by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta.
But Robert Dugger, a partner at the hedge fund Tudor Investment Corp, was more comfortable with emerging market investment values.
Alluding to a speech by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan recently, Dugger said he saw no sign of "irrational exuberance" in emerging markets.
